newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch ministry to probe TV claims on El-Al crash.
newsitem.headline: Dutch ministry to probe TV claims on El-Al crash.

text.p: The Dutch transport ministry said on Friday it would investigate television claims that two separate sets of air weigh-bill documents exist for the El-Al freighter which crashed into a block of flats in Amsterdam four years ago killing at least 42 people.
Ministry spokesman Ton van Wijk told Reuters that a probe would be launched following a NOVA documetary screened on Dutch television on Thursday evening.
The programme featured a report which showed that two weigh-bills were in circulation which the documentary makers claimed had been provided by the Israeli national carrier.
A month ago, the transport ministry had asked El-Al to provide weigh-bill papers relating to flight TY1862, which crashed into an Amsterdam suberb in 1992.
After studying the documents, Transport Minister Annemarie Jorritsma said there was no evidence to re-open an investigation into the causes of the accident.
There has been speculation that the two separate sets of papers show a discrepancy in the number of cargo lots on board the ill-fated freight liner.
Van Wijk said in a telephone interview that the claims made in the NOVA documentary were "very strange".
"We're having meetings about this today, and an investigation will follow," he said.
